item.title: C++ Include Source Files vs. Header Files: Performance and Linking Implications
item.description:
“C++ Include Source Files vs. Header Files: Performance and Linking Implications”

When developing in C or C++, developers often separate code into header files (.h or .hpp) for declarations and source files (.cpp) for definitions. What occurs, technically and practically, when one decides to use #include on a .cpp file instead of a header file, and what are the downstream effects on compilation speed and program architecture?

The Preprocessor’s Role and Translation Units

The C++ standard dictates that #include directs the preprocessor to literally copy the content of the specified file into the current translation unit before compilation begins.

item.title: When to Use the Builder Design Pattern for Object Creation
item.description:
“When to Use the Builder Design Pattern for Object Creation”

When constructing objects with numerous parameters, especially those with many optional configurations, the Builder design pattern offers a structured and readable approach. It separates the construction of a complex object from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create different representations. This pattern is particularly beneficial when a class has multiple constructors or when the object’s creation logic is intricate.
